survey: Spring-rider duck on sand. The duck body is one moulded shell. Its flat underside sits on a blue round mounting plate. A single steel coil spring runs from that plate down to a recessed collar on a square blue base, which lies flat on the sand with a contact shadow. A red handle bar passes crosswise through the neck. The long end sticks out on the near side and a short stub shows on the far side, which fits a through-bar seen at three-quarter angle. A red seat patch sits on the back between the neck and the raised tail. The wing is raised moulding on the body side. The eye faces the camera at an angle (ratio 0.83, near a true ellipse), as expected for a side-turned head. There are no footrests. That is an acceptable simplification, because the rider can still sit, hold the handle and rock. Every part attaches: body to spring plate, spring to base, base to ground, handle through neck. Nothing floats, and there are no loose ends or invented parts.
